task:
Galaxy map renderer: split Finder result markers from catalogue stars so the density cross-fade only affects catalogue stars (review finding M05). apps/web only.

VERIFIED ON MAIN (e3aba577): `apps/web/src/lib/spatial/babylon/adapter.ts` `applyDensityCrossfade()` shares one `starMesh`/StandardMaterial between FINDER results and CATALOGUE viewport stars. When any Finder instances are present (`product.starMeshHasFinderInstances`) the whole mesh is forced to alpha 1, so keeping one search result visible also brings back every catalogue star at wide zoom; with no Finder rows the whole mesh fades. Selection/result changes therefore change thousands of unrelated markers with the camera unchanged. Accent rings (`setStellarAccentAlpha`) and pickability (`setStarPickable`) follow the same single alpha.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Render catalogue stars and Finder result/selected markers as independent thin-instance batches (two meshes with their own materials, or one mesh with per-instance alpha if the existing material path supports it reliably on both WebGPU and WebGL2 — prefer two meshes). Catalogue stars follow the density cross-fade alpha and pickability as today; Finder results and the selected/reference markers stay at full opacity and remain pickable regardless of zoom.
2. Stellar accent rings (black-hole halos etc.) follow the alpha of the batch their star belongs to.
3. Picking: exact ray picks and the nearest-projected-star fallback must consider both batches, with Finder/selected markers taking priority on a tie; a faded catalogue batch must not intercept picks. Preserve identity (system id64) through rendering, picking and labels.
4. Preserve the existing layer receipts and `spatialLayer` metadata contracts; add the batch split to the receipt if the receipt shape allows (counts per batch) without breaking existing consumers.
5. Do not change thresholds, palette, glyphs, star geometry or labels in this task.

TESTS (vitest, `babylon/adapter.test.ts` with the existing NullEngine test support): with density present and camera at a density-dominant distance, catalogue batch alpha < 1 while the Finder batch alpha == 1; adding/removing one Finder result does not change catalogue batch alpha; pick at a Finder marker resolves to its id64 while the catalogue batch is faded; accent ring alpha follows its batch; receipts unchanged for existing fields. Existing adapter tests must keep passing.

VALIDATION: in apps/web run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`. CHANGES.md: one dated 2026-11-02 entry at the top; say this is a visible rendering change that needs Product E2E/visual validation before production promotion and is not deployed.
